issues.legal_issue: A contested will is duly proved only when the statutory requirements for its execution and proof are established; registration alone does not establish due execution.
material_facts: The will was contested, and the two attesting witnesses gave contradictory accounts about whether the testator signed the will and whether they signed it in the testator’s presence.
The registrar’s endorsement established that the witnesses signed the endorsement in the testator’s presence, but did not establish the attestation required for due execution of the will.
The will was registered, but the trial court found due execution unproved and the first appellate court affirmed that finding.
issues.conclusion: Due execution of the will was not proved; its registration did not cure the failure of proof.
issues.legal_principle: Section 63 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925 requires attestation by at least two witnesses in the manner it specifies. Under Section 68 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, at least one available and capable attesting witness must be called to prove execution of a document required by law to be attested. The proviso to Section 68 concerning registered documents does not apply to wills. The court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.contested_will_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a dispute over whether a will was duly executed.
predicates.attesting_witnesses_contradict_each_othe: The attesting witnesses give conflicting accounts about the testator’s signing or the witnesses’ attestation in the testator’s presence.
predicates.required_attestation_unproved: The evidence does not establish that the testator and witnesses completed the required acts of signing or acknowledgment and attestation.
predicates.registrar_endorsement_proves_only_endors: The registration-related endorsement establishes only that witnesses signed the endorsement in the testator’s presence, not that the will was duly attested.

issues.definition: When a will is disputed and the evidence does not establish the required acts of execution and attestation, contradictory witness accounts or an endorsement proving only its own signing leave the will unproved.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that a will was duly executed cannot be sustained where the evidence contradicts due execution and the assessment overlooks circumstances that cast suspicion on the will.
material_facts: The trial court found that due execution of the will was not proved, and the first appellate court affirmed that finding.
The High Court reversed those findings after reassessing the evidence, relying in part on the testator’s legal-clerk occupation and the interval between execution and death.
The legatee actively participated in the will’s execution, and the will made no provision for either of the testator’s two widows, including one unrelated to the legatee.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s decision was set aside, and the trial court’s decree as affirmed by the first appellate court was restored.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing due execution, the court must consider the evidence and the totality of the circumstances, including circumstances creating suspicion. The court considered the legatee’s active participation and the omission of provision for both widows; it cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_reversal_of_concurrent_will_finding and attesting_witnesses_contradict_each_other and legatee_active_in_execution and widows_unprovided_for

predicates.appeal_from_reversal_of_concurrent_will_: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision that reversed concurrent lower-court findings on whether a will was duly executed.
predicates.attesting_witnesses_contradict_each_othe: The attesting witnesses give conflicting accounts about the execution and attestation of the will.
predicates.legatee_active_in_execution: The person benefiting under the will actively participated in its execution.
predicates.widows_unprovided_for: The will makes no provision for the testator’s widows.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a reversal of concurrent findings against due execution, contradictory attesting-witness accounts, active participation by the beneficiary, and omission of provision for the widows mean the reversal is not sustained.
